video.title: The most expensive software bug in history...

protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: The whole bug story, which cannot land shorter: a dead 2003 feature flag triggering the aggressive-buying test function Power Peg was reused for the new Retail Liquidity Program; deployment by hand ('Pony Express') reached only 7 of 8 servers; the eighth woke up Power Peg; Knight rolled back the seven healthy servers so all eight ran it; payoff at 242.8: 45 minutes, 4 million trades, a $7B position. Every step is needed setup, so it runs ~102s (over band). 231.5 (the Power Peg name joke) is an acceptable earlier end; 256.3 adds the $440M loss after the Wizard Software aside. Knight is only named mid-clip, but the story reads as a software-bug tale without it.

also_ok.why: Cold open: 'software has always been held together with duct tape and the poverty of open-source maintainers', then Knight Capital, 10% of US stock trading, lost $440M in 45 minutes and was sold for parts four months later. A strong surprising fact, but it is a teaser that raises 'how?' without answering, so acceptable rather than required. Starting at 0.1 (the list of recent AI-era security incidents) also works as the hook; the range spans both, shorter preferred.

negatives.why: Intro teaser: 'learn how to lose $10 million in a minute with this one weird trick', date, Code Report.
Exposition on Knight as market maker, 'citadel of its time', SMARS order router 'printed money' -- lively but background with no payoff.
NYSE Retail Liquidity Program setup and 'Just kidding, they did it in the most lazy way possible' -- a joke whose payoff is the story that follows.
Aftermath: Wizard Software $3 to $14, $440M down, stock -75%, sold to Getco, 'nothing bad ever happened again' -- big numbers whose support came in the previous minute.
Hyperagent sponsor read, opening with a tempting 'three people drowning in a thousand GitHub issues about daylight savings' line.
